ANSWER: DO NOT COST IT AND DO NOT RUN IT AS WRITTEN. Holding the network fixed removes the measured leg's ONLY path to the extracted cross section, so the arm cannot observe information loss -- the very quantity the proposal exists to isolate. Its two declared outcomes are not two measurements; one is unreachable and the other is guaranteed by construction.
A_REPAIR_THAT_MIGHT_WORK_not_costed_not_: OBSERVATION, MINE, OFFERED AS A DIRECTION AND NOT A PROPOSAL. The incompatibility is structural: the measured leg enters only through step-1 training, so ANY arm that fixes the whole network necessarily kills the data channel. Fixing STEP 2 ONLY while refitting STEP 1 would let resampled data flow into the step-1 weights while removing the step-2 refit -- a different decomposition that does not zero the channel of interest. It would cost most of a training per replica, so it is not the cheap route, and I have not costed it, checked its runnability, or verified that step 1 and step 2 are separable in this codebase. Whether it isolates what OI-126 needs is a physics question for B/C, not mine.

A_ROUTE_THAT_MAY_ALREADY_BE_DECLARED_add.why_it_discriminates_where_the_fixed_net: The fixed-net arm removes the REFIT and thereby also removes the data channel, because the measured leg reaches the result only through training. That isolates refit sensitivity DIRECTLY without touching the data channel, and it is subtractable from the family spread. floor spread ~ family spread in the band  => the 67% is refit sensitivity  => branch (b). floor spread << family spread             => the excess is data-driven  => branch (a). STEP_1_WHAT_IT_PROPOSES_IN_ITS_OWN_TERMS: Keep Poisson(1) rather than substituting a noise model. Propagate the Poisson(1) resampling of the MEASURED leg through a FIXED, already-trained network (the nominal's) instead of refitting per replica, then compare the fixed-net spread against the existing 50-replica refit spread. Declared readout: spreads comparable => information loss => C_stat valid and the band's uncertainties simply large (branch a); fixed-net spread much smaller => the excess is refit sensitivity, an estimator defect (branch b).

THE_DEFECT_verified_in_code.claim: With the network FIXED, the measured-leg Poisson draw has NO path to the extracted xsec. The only per-replica quantity that survives to the result is the SIGNAL-MC factor.
evidence: extract_fullevent_replica.py:184-199 -- extract_replica_xsec(inputs_npz, w_push, sig_factor) and the arithmetic is `w_push * sig_factor`. Those are its only per-replica inputs.
extract_fullevent_replica.py:146,157 -- data_factor is computed and hashed into the receipt as data_factor_sha256, and is passed to NOTHING downstream. It never enters the arithmetic.

extract_fullevent_fps.py:257-259 -- w_push = reweight_full_inventory(inputs_npz, contract): 'Evaluate the trained step-2 model on EVERY signal-MC row.' Its inputs are the dump and the TRAINED ARTIFACT. No data leg.

Consistent with BEN-151, which established independently that the data factors are persisted nowhere and compared nowhere, and that the loader telemetry has sig_ and bkg_ entries and no data equivalent.
THE_DEFECT_verified_in_code.inference: A fixed network means one `contract` for every replica, so `w_push` is IDENTICAL across the arm. The measured leg reaches the result only by having shaped the training, and the training is precisely what this proposal removes. What the arm would measure is signal-MC Poisson spread under the nominal's weights -- a real quantity, and not the one asked for.

THE_PROPOSAL_ALSO_FORBIDS_ITS_OWN_COSTIN: Its section 'What must be settled before it is proposed for real' states verbatim: 'None of this is done, and the proposal should not be costed until it is.' Four preconditions, none met. Item 1 is runnability (explicitly unchecked). ITEM 3 is the one that matters here: 'whether the comparison is coherent under the C_stat contract... is a spec question, not a compute question', and lane C never ruled on the analogous question for the retired contrast. The header says NOT COSTED and RUNNABILITY EXPLICITLY UNCHECKED. I was asked to do the thing the artifact says not to do yet, and the artifact's reason turns out to be the right one.
WHAT_I_DID_NOT_DO_AND_WHY: I did not produce a GPU/CPU price. Costing an instrument that cannot answer the question would have produced exactly the trap the dispatch warned about -- 'affordable has been the tell all day, not the recommendation'. A number would have made an unsound arm look decision-ready. No pin sweep either: BEN-386's ceiling is that a sweep can only ever show expense, never cheapness, and the blocking constraint here is upstream of runnability.
WHAT_THIS_DOES_AND_DOES_NOT_LICENSE: It does NOT answer OI-126 and I am not claiming it does. Whether a Gate-6-shaped floor is comparable to the C_stat family spread under the C_stat contract is item 3 of the fixed-net proposal's precondition list and is lane C's spec question on any route. What it DOES do is move the ask from 'design and run a new instrument' to 'the per-cell floor already exists, here are its numbers, and here are the four reasons it is not a drop-in'. Also live and recorded in 56863958 itself: FLOOR_INTERMEDIATE fired neither predeclared branch, so a C_stat floor could land in the same declared middle and leave OI-126's binary exactly where it is, minus the compute.

WHY_BOTH_OUTCOMES_ARE_UNSOUND.fixed-net spread much smaller (read as b: GUARANTEED BY CONSTRUCTION. An entire variance source was ZEROED rather than isolated, so a smaller spread is what the design produces regardless of whether refit sensitivity exists. This is the same shape as BEN-250 and BEN-186: a check whose result is fixed before the data is seen.
WHY_BOTH_OUTCOMES_ARE_UNSOUND.net: The arm is biased toward branch (b) by construction and cannot support branch (a). A biased instrument on a binary decision with OPPOSITE publication consequences is worse than no instrument, because it returns an answer.
WHY_BOTH_OUTCOMES_ARE_UNSOUND.spreads comparable (read as branch a): UNREACHABLE as evidence for information loss. It could only occur if signal-MC Poisson fluctuation ALONE reproduced the 67% band spread. That would be a genuine and surprising finding, but it is a statement about MC statistics, not about whether the MEASURED leg constrains the region -- which is what 'information loss' denotes in the proposal's own definition at its line 10-11.
